The slopes of a generalised ordered logit by threshold

Source: R/gol.R
gocoef.Rd

The coefficients of gologt() laid out as a table: one row per threshold of the outcome, one column per term, so that a covariate's slopes can be read across the cuts of the scale (a parallel covariate repeats its one slope), with their standard errors and, for the free covariates, the Wald test that the slopes are equal.

Usage

gocoef(object, v = NULL)

Arguments

object

A result of gologt().

v

NULL for every term, or the names of terms: "(Intercept)" and the covariates.

Value

A list: est and se, matrices with one row per threshold (named as "low|med") and one column per term of v; wald, the rows of the fit's Wald tests for the covariates of v.

See also

gologt().

Examples

set.seed(8)
n <- 300
d <- data.frame(race = rbinom(n, 1, 0.4), age = rnorm(n))
u <- runif(n)
d$risk <- 1 + (u < plogis(0.5 + 0.8 * d$race)) +
  (u < plogis(-1 + 0.1 * d$race - 0.3 * d$age))
gocoef(gologt(d, "risk", c("race", "age")), "race")
#> $est
#>            race
#> 1|2  0.69848026
#> 2|3 -0.03629893
#> 
#> $se
#>          race
#> 1|2 0.2765599
#> 2|3 0.2509516
#> 
#> $wald
#>   term     stat df          p
#> 1 race 6.354064  1 0.01171127
#>
